Basis: the principle on the blocked side, 8187310f ("It never takes in a fee that was charged contrary to those rules: the fee balance a payoff settles is made up only of fees the rules support"), and its definition ("a fee leaves it when it is settled out of a payment or when a waiver of it is recorded. It is taken as it stands at the moment the payoff figure is set"); the depended-on rules, a0e51984 + 9b3bba79 + 53186876 + 0ef1f26f; records. Strength: hard in both source and KB. Condition stated in any document: **no**. Depended-on documents restating the payoff principle: **no** (none of a0e51984 / 9b3bba79 / 53186876 / 0ef1f26f mentions a payoff).
- **E-P2: `auto_ext_payoff_settlement` <- `auto_ext_closed_source_late_charge_waiver`** (value_input, gate fees_due). The same basis with ba913bda + 4dc930d3 + 1b2a81b3 + 27af4ea3. Hard strength, matches. Not stated. Depended-on documents do not restate the payoff principle.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION PASS.** Every atom of the three claimed extended policies, their governing base policies, the parameters read and the three tool contracts has one equivalent home. The two declared prerequisites are entailed at hard strength from the principle on the blocked side, the depended-on rules and the records, and neither is stated anywhere. Nothing is added or changed in meaning. First revision; none precede it.

## explicitness

Blind hop marks (task 1 item 6): P1 identification derived, P2 identification derived, P1->R and P2->R derived (with a borderline note on how compactly 8187310f states the principle next to its definition; no sentence names the waivers or a gate). No hop is read off. No title or opening mirrors the task: "Auto Loans: Fees Settled by a Payoff", "Auto Loans: Paying Off a Loan from PCB Checking", "Auto Loans: Bank-Error Waiver of Returned Payment Fees", "Auto Loans: Bank-Error Waiver of Late Charges" and the rest name general subjects. There is no named mistake, wrong-vs-right contrast, or cross-problem example.

Wording-level findings:

- **E1 — charter sentence copied.** a0e51984 "Why it is the bank's error": "PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a paying account that is open on each debit date." Source `auto_ext_closed_source_returned_fee_waiver.rule`: "PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a source account that is open on each debit date". One word differs. The next sentence, "The requirement that an autopay paying account be an active checking account of the borrower, which applies when autopay is set up, therefore also applies to every later debit", stays close to the charter's "extending to every debit the enrollment-time requirement that the autopay source be an active checking account of the borrower". The opening of "When the waiver is owed" reuses the charter run "that PCB presented to a PCB checking account".
- **E2 — the same phrasing recurs across documents.** "only on a paying account that is open on each debit date" appears in both a0e51984 and ba913bda ("An autopay enrollment at PCB draws only on a paying account that is open on each debit date"). Both hubs also share "contrary to the Auto Loans rules when" and "… of the waived sum credited to principal because the …".
- **E3 — templated section openings and wording across sibling documents (minor).** 57c89913 and 4befbdc7 share the section frame "When this applies — The service answers a borrower's request … by transfer from a PCB checking account …" and their parameter/receipt rows. 27af4ea3 and 0ef1f26f share the opening "This rule gives the sum waived when a …". 53186876 and 1b2a81b3 share "and the PCB checking account it was drawn on" / "the account was still open on the". 4dc930d3 and 9b3bba79 share "booked on the loan, ranked by posting date". Several of these runs are close to fixed phrases. They are listed because the template recurs.

**KB-EXPLICIT RED — E1, E2, E3.** These are wording-level only: no dependency, order or procedure is stated, and every hop of task 1's tree must be derived. The machine gate reported "no copied or templated wording" at its threshold, and this finding is the manual judgement beyond that gate.

## source-layer notes (reported, not re-judged here)

- **S1 (task tool vs base trigger).** `post_payoff_payment_63569e96` books `payment_channel="pcb_transfer"` but does not debit the checking account, although base `auto_evt_payment_allocation` says "Payments from a PCB checking account debit that account through the payment's trigger" (trigger `checking:checking_debit`) and b9b5eac7 renders it faithfully. Nature: the tool implementation omits a side effect the base declares. The defect is in `task_tools.py`, not in the blueprint base section. No scored value moves (the GT is replayed through the same tool; the funds test reads the ledger before the payoff).
- **S4 ("every" vs "most recent").** `auto_ext_payoff_settlement` says "every returned payment fee … / every late charge … is waived … before the payoff amount is fixed". The waiver policies' computes examine only the most recent returned_payment fee / late_charge (`LATEST(...)`). In a world with two contrary fees of one kind, the payoff principle (8187310f) would require both to be removed while each waiver rule identifies only the latest. This is a latent source-side tension. The KB carries both sides faithfully and does not resolve it. In task 1 only the most recent fee of each kind is contrary (the 2025 fees were charged while the account was open and are settled), so no scored value moves.
- Base section of blueprint/: no defect found in the base policies governing this task. The due-date-window note in task 0's file does not bear on this task.
